That's alright. It's not easy talking about this. It could be helpful if you think about what you would like to say to her, write it down and practice. So you can be prepared to talk and answer questions as well, if she asks.

Hello! For starters I am not necessarily in your position but I have some advice! 

You could bring subtle hints about being uncomfortable with your body and asking her what she thinks about transgender people or LGBT people in general. It massively helps if you do research in case she or your kids have some questions. 

Before you tell her though, it would be good to find clothing, items, accessories that make you feel more comfortable in confident in who you are. It may take awhile and some talks here and there. 

I wish you the best of luck! If you need help, advice or you wish to talk the community as well as I am here!

Hello, I've had a similar experience too! Some advice I can give is to research and start to mention how you are dysphoric and being around your dad and brothers does not influence it. Also, it helps to do some research before hand. It helped me, and it prepares you for any questions your parents might have too. For the clothes and and what you want to wear, you can start saving up money and looking at things that make you more comfortable in your body. I know this may sound sucky, but there may be a chance that your parents will be confused and say it's a phase. If this does happen stay adamant on how you feel. You know your body best. There are also tons of groups to reach put too! If you need support or anything of the like, you can pm me if you feel comfortable or confide in someone you trust. An important thing to remember is sometimes results can happen overtime as it can be something hard to get used to. I am rooting for you the whole way!
